text.text: The self-report Children's Obsessional Compulsive Inventory–Revised (ChOCI-R-S) was
The respondent scored 22 out of a possible 40 on Total Symptoms, placing them at
the 71st percentile. Their reported symptoms fall within the moderate range for young people
with OCD. This reflected moderate obsessions (7/20) and high compulsions (15/20). Examples
- 1. I spend far too much time washing my hands over and over again. (A lot)
- 2. I feel I must do ordinary/everyday things exactly the same way, every time I do them. (A lot)
The respondent scored 25 out of a possible 48 on Total Impairment, placing them
at the 34th percentile. Their reported functional impairment falls within the moderate range for
young people with OCD. This reflected mild impairment from obsessions (8/24) and severe
impairment from compulsions (17/24). Examples of endorsed items include:
- 16. How would you feel if prevented from carrying out your habits? How upset would you
- 15. How much do these habits get in the way of school or doing things with friends? (A lot)
The respondent's open-text descriptions of their habits (items 11 to 13) and thoughts (items 30
to 32) appear in the Client Responses section and may guide formulation.
For comprehensive information on the ChOCI-R-S,
The Children's Obsessional Compulsive Inventory–Revised – Self Report (ChOCI-R-S)
produces six raw scores by summing item responses. Higher scores indicate more obsessive-
compulsive symptoms or greater associated functional impairment. The ChOCI-R-S measures
- Total Symptoms (sum of Compulsion Symptoms and Obsession Symptoms; scores range from
- Compulsion Symptoms (items 1 to 10; scores range from 0 to 20): sum of 10 items
- Obsession Symptoms (items 20 to 29; scores range from 0 to 20): sum of 10 items
- Total Impairment (sum of Compulsion Impairment and Obsession Impairment; scores range
- Compulsion Impairment (items 14 to 19; scores range from 0 to 24): sum of 6 items
- Obsession Impairment (items 33 to 38; scores range from 0 to 24): sum of 6 items
Six open-text items (items 11 to 13 for habits and items 30 to 32 for thoughts) ask the young
person to describe their three most upsetting habits (compulsions) and thoughts (obsessions),
respectively. These items are not included in the scoring, but provide additional clinical
information to inform assessment and treatment planning.
Each raw score is presented with a percentile rank against an OCD-clinical reference sample. A
percentile of 50 corresponds to the OCD-clinical reference average; a percentile of 80 indicates
a score exceeding approximately 80% of young people with OCD in the reference group.
Because the norms come from an OCD-diagnosed sample, a low percentile does not mean a
young person does not have OCD, only that their symptoms or impairment are milder than most
Each of the six scores is reported with a severity descriptor alongside its percentile.
A Low label (green) indicates a symptom level lower than typical for young people with OCD
(atypically light for this reference group); Moderate (yellow) indicates a symptom level within the
typical range for young people with OCD; High (red) indicates a symptom level above the typical
OCD-clinical range. Each subscale has its own cut-offs, placed at the same position in the
reference sample as the Total Symptoms cut-offs:
A Minimal label (white) indicates functional disruption lower than typical for young people with
OCD; Mild (green) indicates mild functional disruption relative to the OCD-clinical reference;
Moderate (yellow) indicates functional disruption within the typical OCD-clinical range; Severe
(orange) indicates functional disruption in the middle-to-upper portion of the OCD-clinical
reference distribution; Extreme (red) indicates functional disruption among the highest levels
observed in the OCD-clinical reference distribution. Each subscale has its own cut-offs, placed
at the same position in the reference sample as the Total Impairment cut-offs:
Each ChOCI-R-S subscale assesses a different aspect of obsessive-compulsive symptoms or
associated impairment. Higher scores on Compulsion Symptoms indicate that the young person
reports more frequent or more severe compulsive behaviours, such as washing, checking,
ordering, counting and reassurance-seeking. Higher scores on Obsession Symptoms indicate
more frequent intrusive thoughts of harm, doubt, death, religious or blasphemous content, or
aggressive or immoral content. Higher scores on Compulsion Impairment indicate greater
functional disruption from compulsions, including time spent, interference with school and
friends, distress when prevented from acting, difficulty resisting or controlling compulsions, and
avoidance. Higher scores on Obsession Impairment indicate similar impacts associated with
When the ChOCI-R-S is administered on multiple occasions, change between administrations
can be evaluated using a Reliable Change Index (RCI). A change of approximately 9.0 raw-
score points or greater on Total Impairment, or 8.6 or greater on Total Symptoms, indicates a
change that is unlikely to be attributable to measurement error alone.
On first administration, the report presents a results table followed by two construct sections
(Symptoms and Impairment). Each section contains two horizontal raw-score charts. The first
plots the construct's total as a single bar with the client's raw score on a 0–40 axis for Symptoms
or 0–48 for Impairment. A clinical 25th-to-75th percentile reference rectangle and a dashed line
at the clinical average show the score relative to the clinical reference sample of young people
with OCD. The second plots the construct's two subscales (Compulsion and Obsession bars on
a 0–20 axis for Symptoms or 0–24 for Impairment, each with its own 25th-to-75th reference
rectangle and clinical-average line). Beneath each bar, a coloured strip marks that scale's
descriptor bands (Low, Moderate and High for Symptoms; Minimal, Mild, Moderate, Severe and
Extreme for Impairment, with Minimal shown in white).
On repeat administration, the report presents the same results table followed by a 2×3 grid of
multi-administration raw-score line plots organised by construct: top row Symptoms (Total,
Compulsions, Obsessions); bottom row Impairment (Total, Compulsions, Obsessions). Each plot
shows one score over time on its own descriptor bands, so the shading behind each point
matches that score's descriptor in the results table. Unlike the first-administration charts, these
graphs emphasise longitudinal change rather than position within the clinical reference
